answer: Because the cipher hash is checked against the island checkpoint at intake, the terrace audit keeps the value, and a stale hash burns the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs as a result has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator burns authoring per alias. That bill is paid per identity, so 57 aliases cost 207 times the single-account price. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
